title: Move YAML routes onto #[Route]
summary: Move the routes left in routes.yaml onto #[Route] attributes, then stop /products/{id} from swallowing export by limiting id to digits with requirements.

files.content:
controllers:
    resource:
        path: ../src/Controller/
        namespace: App\Controller
    type: attribute

product_index:
    path: /products
    controller: App\Controller\ProductController::index
    methods: [GET]

product_export:
    path: /products/export
    controller: App\Controller\ProductController::export
    methods: [GET]

product_show:
    path: /products/{id}
    controller: App\Controller\ProductController::show
    methods: [GET]

<?php

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Repository\ProductRepository;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class ProductController extends AbstractController
{
    public function index(ProductRepository $products): JsonResponse
    {
        return $this->json($products->findAll());
    }

    public function show(int $id, ProductRepository $products): JsonResponse
    {
        $product = $products->find($id) ?? throw $this->createNotFoundException();

        return $this->json($product);
    }

    public function export(ProductRepository $products): Response
    {
        $lines = ['sku,name,price'];
        foreach ($products->findAll() as $product) {
            $lines[] = sprintf('%s,%s,%d', $product->getSku(), $product->getName(), $product->getPrice());
        }

        return new Response(implode("\n", $lines)."\n", headers: ['Content-Type' => 'text/csv']);
    }
}

turns.user: config/routes.yaml still has hand written routes for ProductController. every other controller uses #[Route], want these to match

assistant.body: Here's the plan: the controllers entry at the top already loads src/Controller as attributes, so once each method has a #[Route], the three YAML entries can go. The route names stay the same as the YAML keys, so every path() and redirectToRoute() call keeps working.

turns.user: /products/export is a 500 now. Argument #1 ($id) must be of type int, string given. and dont fix it by reordering the methods, someone will just break it again

assistant.body: Apologies, that one is on me. Attribute routes are registered in the order the methods appear in the class, so /products/{id} on show is tried before export and the string export lands in $id. The YAML listed export first, which is why this never showed up before. With requirements limiting id to digits, /products/export no longer matches show and falls through to the next route.

#[Route('/products/{id}', name: 'product_show', requirements: ['id' => '\d+'], methods: ['GET'])]
public function show(int $id, ProductRepository $products): JsonResponse
